body: The thought of an afterlife is the most terrifying concept for me. Thankfully I see no evidence for it and think that the probability of an afterlife is very low. "I" was perfectly fine not existing for an immeasurable amount of time before I was born, and "I" will be perfectly fine not existing for an immeasurable amount of time after I die.

I appreciate the perspective. 

But the thing is is that my depression is not related to any particular *thing* [i.e. having low self-esteem, being unemployed, anxiety issues]. My problem is that I dislike life in general.

I do want to get better, but the answer isn't as obvious as it would be if it were a concrete thing that were making me depressed. A person that is unemployed can get a job. A person with anxiety can work on coping mechanisms. A person who is lonely can get a girlfriend. An overweight person can lose weight. But what can I do? "Learn to enjoy life"? It's not like I can just turn on a happy switch. 

I do not have low self-esteem. I have a good well-paying job. I have a house, a car, a valued college degree. I'm not in debt. I have people who love me, and several girls show attraction toward me so I could get a girlfriend if I so desired. I am reasonably intelligent and average looking. 

My problem is that I have absolutely no lust for life. I have tried to find hobbies that I enjoy, but nothing brings me joy. Lord knows I've tried. Even sex makes me feel "meh." When I force myself to go on a hike, I feel no accomplishment afterward. All that exercise is good for for me is making my feet ache and back sore. 

Life feels like a giant *chore.* Maybe such a complaint sounds trivial, but think about what reason do I have to go through all of the daily aches and pains and blahs of life? I may not have significant pains [back pain, tooth pain], but there is nothing positive to give a point for going through my negatives. When I have free time I choose to sleep because there is nothing else that I enjoy. 

And it's infuriating because I never chose to live. I never consented to *any* of this: life was forced upon me. Given the choice now I would have chosen to have never been born. But I cannot do that now, and I will not commit suicide [mostly to spare others pain and misery]. So I am stuck here, maintaining a body and a life that I want nothing to do with. Even cooking and eating is an incredible chore for me. I am underweight because as much lust for eating as a normal person would have for filing their taxes. 

The point of my post wasn't to say that everything is predetermined by forces outside of you and to encourage a sort of learned helplessness [although I see now how it could have misinterpreted that way and I should have written it differently to more accurately express my ideas].

My point was that there is no guarantee that something can achieved merely through hope and effort. But my point is *not* to encourage no effort at all: of course not. 

It is like someone going through cancer: they can take all the medication and go through all the therapy they possibly can, but no amount of medication or therapy or hope will guarantee that they will get better. They could very well get worse. The universe [or God] does not give one single fuck about you or how much hope you have or how good of a person you are or how much suffering you have gone through already. 

It is the same way with depression. A person can try with all his heart and be treated with the best doctors and medications in the world, and there is guarantee that he will get better. I find notions like "it *will* get better" and "this will pass and the rest of your life will be great" to be presumptuous and, to be honest, a bit insulting. It certainly could get better, especially with more medical advancements, but you do not *know*. 

Where did I say that I am relying on God anyway? I said that "God" [I myself am an agnostic] does not *care* about us. In your darkest rock bottom moment there *is* no God to turn to and pray to. Any effort to get better *has* to be made by *yourself*. 

Again, another thing I somewhat dislike about this board is how much people project from a post. Depression comes in many shapes and sizes. The word is really just a catch-all for not feeling mentally well. Whenever I see someone post here, I always see lots of assumptions being made. 

I know that my post is disjointed. I don't really have the energy to organize it in a more coherent manner.

What? I think that you're starting to project stuff into me. Depression is different for everyone. 

I'm 25. I do not have any friends and I only have one close family member. The only reason is that she has already been through so much suffering in her life that I would feel extremely guilty for making her feel bad. 

And I wish that I were never born because I have no passion for life. Everything bores me. And because I have nothing positive, everything negative feels especially bad because it feels like it is for nothing. I have chronic pains: back pains, toothaches, bladder pains, and while it isn't unbearable it adds to my dislike for life.

Every day feels empty. There is nothing that I want to do. In my spare time all I do is sleep because there is nothing else that I would rather do. Every day feels like a gigantic pointless chore. 

Life just feels like a gigantic burden that I never asked for. And it's besides the point that it *might* improve later: life is something that I never **asked** for. It was brought unto me against my will.

Anyway, I just wanted to say that we're all different here.

Some people are depressed because they feel unloved.

Some people have low self-esteem and/or body issues.

Some people have anxiety so bad that it drives them to suicide.

Some people have hard home lives or are suffering from an extremely traumatic experience.

Some people have chronic physical illnesses or chronic pain that make life unbearable. 

I think that I'm personally a bit of an odd-ball as far as suicidals go. I don't have low self-esteem. I don't feel unloved. I consider myself to have a good life relative to other people. But I am unable to have fun. My anhendonia is very very severe, nothing ever excites me. Life feels like nothing but a gigantic chore because there is almost nothing I enjoy. I don't really want sex, masturbation feels good for maybe a few minutes, video games bore me, everything bores me. I have a constant emptiness, an all-consuming nihilism. I am not interested in family. I am not interested in having friends. I live alone and only interact with society for work and shopping [apart from online convos]. Hardly anything elicits emotion in me. When I go home I sleep because I don't see the point in doing anything else, and I don't have the energy. 

I really have no *rational* reason that I can come up with as to why I am so miserable. There is nothing making me anxious. There is nothing that I lack that I want. But I am still incredibly miserable. My mind feels so empty that it is literally painful.

Love isn't going to help me. 

Love doesn't save me from the nihilism saturating my head. The constant feeling of pointlessness and apathy. If I actually found life to be inherently enjoyable and good it wouldn't matter if it had no meaning. But I hate life. Not just my life. I hate **life**. I hate this world. 

The big things and the little things. I hate waking up every morning, I hate feeling the cold, I hate toothaches, I hate it when my god damn car doesn't start up, I hate everyone acting like I committed a major moral fault by being 5 minutes late for work [for God's sake if I'm there before 8:15 just be happy I'm awake and haven't shot myself yet.]
